Author: Ravindra Maithani

High Court Of Uttarakhand At Nainital
 First Bail Application No.749 of 2023
Karan ........Applicant
 Versus
State of Uttarakhand ........Respondent
Present:-
 Mr. Prince Chauhan, Advocate for the applicant.
 Mr. B.C. Joshi, A.G.A. for the State.

entities.text: High Court Of Uttarakhand At Nainital
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)

Applicant Karan is in judicial custody in Case Crime No. 294 of 2022, under Section 363, 366, 376
(2)
(n) Ipc and Section 3(a)/4 and 5 (l) /6 of the Protection of Children From Sexual Offences Act,
2012, Police Station Bahadrabad, District Haridwar.
He has sought his release on bail.

2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
3.
According to the FIR, the victim a young girl of 16 years was found missing from her sister's house, where she was staying on 01.08.2022 at 11:00 AM.
Subsequently, the victim was recovered.
She revealed that she and the applicant both are in relationship.
She wanted to stay with the applicant.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant would submit that the applicant is 18 years old boy, where as the victim is 16 years of age.
They were in relationship; The victim joined his company and she has stated in her examination under Sections 161 and 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 and to the doctor also.
It is also argued that, in fact, the informant also during investigation, admitted that the victim and the applicant, both were in relationship and they went together.
Although, it is argued that subsequently, the victim changed her stance and has stated against the applicant in her statement given in the court.
5. Learned State counsel would submit that in the court the victim has supported the prosecution case.
Although, he would submit that during investigation, the victim has stated that she was in relationship with the applicant.

sentences.text: 6. Admittedly, the sister of the victim, who is informant has also stated that the applicant and the victim both were in the relationship.

7. In the cases of Mahesh Kumar v. State (NCT of Delhi), 2023 SCC OnLine Del 2634, Faizan Wahid Baig v. The State of Maharashtra, MANU/MHOR/62774/2022, Vijaylakshmi and another v. State and another, 2021 SCC OnLine Mad 317, Shri John Franklin Shylla v. State of Meghalaya & Anr.,
2023 SCC OnLine Megh 303 and Ashik Ramjali Ansari v. State of Maharashtra and another, 2023 SCC OnLine Bom 1390, the Courts have either granted bail or quashed the proceedings or acquitted the accused in the cases like instant one.

sentences.text: 8. Having considered, this Court is of the view that subject to certain conditions, the applicant may be enlarged on bail.
9. The bail application is allowed.

10. Let the applicant be released on bail, on his executing a personal bond and furnishing two reliable sureties, each of the like amount, to the satisfaction of the Court concerned, subject to the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant or any of his relatives shall not make any contact with the victim, in any manner, whatsoever, either physically, electronically or by any other means.
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing the facts to Court or any Police Officer and the applicant should not tamper with evidence.
(Ravindra Maithani, J) 16.05.2024 Jitendra Karan vs State Of Uttarakhand on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127742054/
